title: Letting Go of Shame
note: Turned away and unable to bear it, the man tells her friend he has given up shame. The woman, wanting her love made known, tells her friend the same. This comes when love is at its height.

couplets.plain: For those who suffer and ache with desire, there is no refuge and no strength but the palmyra stalk.
couplets.pm: Men who have enjoyed desire with women hard to reach, and then lost it, suffer. The palmyra stalk, their old protection, is now my only strength, because it brings that joy back and ends the pain. Men have long won joy this way. I counted on you to help me, in vain. Now that I know you won’t, I will win it this way too.
couplets.note: The palmyra stalk, மடல், is the mock horse a spurned lover rides in public to press his claim on a woman.
couplets.context: Turned away by her friend and unable to bear it, he says this to her.
couplets.speaker: he
couplets.sensitive: treats a self-wounding public ordeal as love’s only way out

links.quote: no refuge and no strength but the palmyra stalk
links.reason: Holds up the palmyra stalk as the one refuge left to those who ache with desire.

links.quote: those who suffer and ache with desire
links.reason: Speaks for all who ache with desire, not for himself alone.

couplets.plain: My body and soul, which can’t bear this, will ride the palmyra stalk, putting shame aside.
couplets.pm: My body and soul can’t bear this pain and mean to ride the palmyra horse that protects against it, having put aside the shame that would forbid it. Wisdom, self-control and the rest went first. Shame stayed, and now it has gone too. He says they will ride so that she sees how much he suffers and quickly grants what he asks.
couplets.context: He goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: he
couplets.sensitive: resolves on the self-wounding ride because the pain cannot be borne

couplets.plain: Once I had shame and good manly strength. Today I have the palmyra stalk that people in desire ride.
couplets.pm: Once I had shame and great manliness. Desire has driven them out, and today I have the palmyra stalk ridden by those overcome by desire. Shame stops you doing anything low, and manliness is standing firm before anything. Those were then. This is all I have now, so it will soon be done.
couplets.context: He goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: he
couplets.sensitive: the self-wounding ride is all he says he has left

links.quote: Today I have the palmyra stalk
links.reason: The stalk is now what he has, in place of the shame and manly strength he once had.

couplets.plain: The fierce flood of desire carries off the raft of shame and good manly strength.
couplets.pm: I took shame and manliness as rafts to cross it. The fierce flood of desire tears them from me and carries them off. Other floods can’t do that, which is why he calls this one fierce. They are no rafts for this flood, and so they go.
couplets.context: He goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: he

links.quote: the raft of shame and good manly strength
links.reason: Shame and manly strength were the raft he trusted, and it went with the flood.

couplets.plain: She of the small bangles strung like a garland gave me the palmyra stalk, and the sorrow that comes with the evening.
couplets.pm: I never knew the sorrow of evening, or the stalk that is its medicine. She of the small bangles strung like a garland gave me both. Desire is there at other hours but flowers at evening, and the stalk comes from that, so she gave that disgrace too. She is so young she will say what you tell her. She gave these, so you can remove them.
couplets.context: He goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: he
couplets.sensitive: names the self-wounding ride as what she has left him with

links.quote: the sorrow that comes with the evening

couplets.plain: Even at midnight I think of riding the palmyra stalk. Because of this innocent girl my eyes won’t close.
couplets.pm: Because of your innocent girl my eyes never close in sleep. So even at midnight, when everyone sleeps, I sit up thinking only of riding the stalk. “Innocent” speaks of her simplicity, not her age. Don’t put off what I ask until tomorrow.
couplets.context: He goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: he
couplets.sensitive: a sleepless lover resolves on the self-wounding ride

links.quote: I think of riding the palmyra stalk
links.reason: Sleeplessness keeps his mind on riding the stalk.
Midnight finds him awake, thinking of the ride.

couplets.plain: Nothing is greater than a woman, who suffers desire as vast as the sea and still doesn’t ride the palmyra stalk.
couplets.pm: No birth in the world is as noble as a woman’s. She suffers the sickness of desire, shoreless as the sea, and bears it without riding the stalk. I wasn’t born to that, and you don’t see it. The man’s words end here, and from now on she speaks.
couplets.context: He has blamed his sleeplessness on an innocent girl. Her friend says men have the wisdom women lack, so men should bear it. He answers.
couplets.speaker: he
couplets.sensitive: praises a woman for bearing love’s pain in silence; the ride it names is self-wounding

links.quote: Nothing is greater than a woman
links.reason: Rates nothing above the woman who bears desire without the ride, however vast it is.

links.quote: still doesn’t ride the palmyra stalk
links.reason: The stalk is the step she refuses, whatever desire puts her through.

links.quote: desire as vast as the sea
links.reason: Her desire is measured by the vastness of the sea.

couplets.plain: Desire doesn’t say, “They are too firm to overcome,” or “They deserve pity.” It breaks out of hiding into the open.
couplets.pm: Desire doesn’t fear that women are too firm to be overcome, or pity them as deserving mercy. Even a woman’s desire gets past her hiding and shows in the open, before her father and brothers. Seeming to speak of women in general, she hints that her own desire has grown and that her love must now be made known.
couplets.context: She is guarded more closely and her desire has grown. She says this to her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: It breaks out of hiding into the open
links.reason: Desire heeds neither firmness nor pity, and breaks out of its own hiding.

couplets.plain: Thinking that no one knows, my desire wanders the streets in a daze.
couplets.pm: “I kept quiet before, so no one knows me. Now I will show myself.” With that thought my desire reels through the streets of this town. The daze means whispers, and the wandering means open gossip, and both have come. Now my love must be made known to my family.
couplets.context: She goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

couplets.plain: Fools laugh in front of my eyes, because they haven’t suffered what I have.
couplets.pm: Fools laugh at me, and not just where I can hear it but before my eyes, as they never did before. They do this because they haven’t suffered what I have. She doesn’t know her friend has told of her love, and is hurt that marriage isn’t coming, so she speaks of her as a stranger.
couplets.context: Her friend has told her foster mother of the love, but jokes that she can’t think how to. Hurt, she says this to herself.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: Fools laugh in front of my eyes

ideaLinks.quote: The fierce flood of desire carries off the raft
ideaLinks.reason: The flood of desire sweeps away the shame and strength he trusted, and in K1138 it breaks through her hiding too.
